teams.heading: Jake White says Fiji can be a massive force at 2027 World Cup
teams.body: Jake White wants his best players back for the 2027 World Cup, and Fiji's Europe-based contingent should be available for the November Tests. White, the 2007 World Cup-winning Springbok coach, picked no Europe-based players against Japan and handed out four new caps, saying he wants to get "the best 33 players together" for the tournament in Australia. The three Nations Championship games in Europe, against France, Ireland and Italy, will be the first real test of that plan.

lead.why: The result has already run, but White's plan for Europe-based returns and the 2027 World Cup squad is a fresh angle for fans.

teams.heading: Joe Marchant back in England camp while Seb Atkinson rehabs knee
teams.body: Joe Marchant is back in England colours after being named in Steve Borthwick's 36-player training camp for the autumn Nations Championship matches. The 30-year-old centre has not played for England since the 2023 World Cup, becoming ineligible after joining Stade Français, but he is available again after returning to Sale Sharks. Borthwick faces injury disruption in midfield, with Seb Atkinson limited to knee rehabilitation at the camp. Marchant, with 26 caps, said in September: "I want to play for England, that's what I want to do."

lead.why: A fresh England squad call-up that also flags midfield injury trouble, which matters more to a fan than the routine camp coverage.

teams.heading: Jeremy Ward may need World Rugby permission before playing for France
teams.body: Jeremy Ward is in Fabien Galthié's 42-man squad for the Nations Championship, but the 30-year-old centre only completes his five-year residency in 2027, so he will train with the group without playing against Fiji, the Springboks or Argentina. The bigger obstacle is his 2016 Junior Springboks appearances, which tied him to South Africa under World Rugby rules. France may need England's route for Benhard Janse van Rensburg: a regulations committee clearance. Ward says: "I'm not going to say that if I change my nationality, I'll be in the team."

lead.why: It is a new France squad storyline about a named player, and it turns on whether Les Bleus can use him at all.

teams.heading: Former Ireland prop Phil O'Callaghan dies aged 83 after short illness
teams.body: Phil O'Callaghan, the former Ireland and Munster prop, has died in Dublin at the age of 83 after a short illness. The Dolphin clubman earned 21 caps for Ireland and 34 for Munster across a career that included more than 20 years at Dolphin, and former Ireland captain Terry Kingston led the tributes from his former clubmate. His family, including nephew Mark O'Leary, said they were extremely proud of his achievements with club, province and country. Funeral arrangements have yet to be announced.

lead.why: A fresh, NEW item about a former Ireland cap that fans will want to read, and it is not a club match or a repeat of the squad news already reported.

teams.heading: Italy sit 11th of 12 in the log after three straight defeats
teams.body: Italy go into the South Africa match 11th of 12 in the log, having lost all three games so far. Those three have produced 37 points scored and 131 conceded, a points difference of -94. The last of them was a 10-57 defeat to Australia in Round three. Italy's best-ever world ranking is No. 8, reached in 2007 and 2024.

teams.heading: Two Scotland hopefuls earn call-ups from Glasgow's 24-20 Benetton win
teams.body: Glasgow's 24-20 win in Treviso produced two Scotland hopefuls who have earned call-ups, the Scotsman reports. Jamie Ritchie's 80-minute blindside display, in his first Warriors appearance after eight months of ankle and Achilles trouble, was the eye-catching part. Gregor Townsend was due to make his postponed Nations Championship squad announcement on Monday. The 63-cap former captain is the one to watch as that squad takes shape.

lead.why: It is the only new item in the shortlist and it concerns Scotland's own call-up picture ahead of the Nations Championship.

teams.heading: Rio Dyer and Ben Carter injured in Dragons derby loss to Ospreys
teams.body: Wales wing Rio Dyer and second-row Ben Carter both left the Dragons' derby defeat to the Ospreys injured, and the extent of Dyer's problem is not yet clear. Dyer went off before half-time and Carter was forced out early in the second half with a head injury. Head coach Filo Tiatia called the knee-drop tackle that left centre Fetuli Paea limping off "dangerous", and pointed to three yellow cards for indiscipline. Knee-drop tackles are banned throughout rugby from 1 November.

lead.why: Two Wales internationals were hurt in the derby, and the knee-drop tackle that Dragons coach Filo Tiatia condemned is banned from 1 November.

teams.heading: Contepomi names Montoya back as captain in 33-man London camp squad
teams.body: Julián Montoya is back to captain Los Pumas after missing the home tests against South Africa and Australia, and Felipe Contepomi has named a 33-man squad for the London camp that Americas Rugby News calls his strongest of the year. Marcos Kremer, Justo Piccardo, Mateo Carreras and Bautista Delguy are all in. Hooker Ignacio Ruiz and No. 8 Joaquín Oviedo are out injured. Contepomi confirms the November roster once the three-day camp ends.

lead.why: It is the team's own squad news, and Montoya's return as captain is the sharpest item in the pack.

teams.heading: Australia A's David Feliuai sent off in 61-12 rout of USA
teams.body: Brumbies midfielder David Feliuai was sent off in the 15th minute, yet Australia A still cruised to a 61-12 win over the USA in their opening match in Nashville. Feliuai was first shown yellow for a high shot, then upgraded to red after making contact with an attacker's head, and his side still controlled the game for 80 minutes under Stephen Larkham. Winger Dylan Pietsch scored a double, and Wallabies debutant Harry McLaughlin-Phillips also crossed. The second match is in New Jersey next weekend.

lead.why: It is the only genuinely new item on the shortlist, a result with a red card and a Wallabies debutant, while the Wilson squad stories have already been reported.

teams.heading: Kwagga Smith's Blue Revs contract terminated by mutual agreement, returns to Bulls
teams.body: Kwagga Smith's exit from the Shizuoka Blue Revs is confirmed, with the club saying his contract was terminated by mutual agreement. The two-time World Cup winner spent eight seasons in Japan and is heading home to sign a three-year deal with the Bulls. Smith tore his ACL and meniscus in May, ruling him out for the rest of the 2026 season, and medical experts have since cleared him to return to play at the end of December. The club has paid tribute to him as a key player.

lead.why: It is the one new Japan-league story in the pack, and it removes a Springbok from the Shizuoka Blue Revs squad.

teams.heading: Richie Mo’unga not yet ruled out of Europe tour after calf tear
teams.body: Richie Mo’unga has not yet been ruled out of the Europe tour, offering the All Blacks a possible boost after the injury list grew following the second Bledisloe Cup Test in Sydney. The flyhalf missed both Bledisloe Tests with a calf tear, and his status remains open even as Leroy Carter’s ankle surgery, Shannon Frizell’s knee and Samisoni Taukei’aho’s calf injury have thinned the squad. The tour opens against Scotland, followed by England and Wales before the finals weekend at Twickenham.

lead.why: It is the only current All Blacks item in the shortlist, and the open question over Richie Mo’unga's tour status is a new angle on the injury story already reported.

teams.heading: Kwagga Smith heads home to Bulls on three-year deal after Japan exit
teams.body: Kwagga Smith is heading home, signing a three-year deal with the Bulls after his Japan contract was terminated by mutual agreement with the Shizuoka Blue Revs. The 33-year-old, who tore his ACL and meniscus in May, has been cleared by medical experts to return to play at the end of December. Bulls coach Johan Ackermann, who coached Smith at the Lions, said: "As a youngster, he showed character and fight and integrity." The Blue Revs paid tribute to eight seasons of service in Japan.
